items.title: 11.2 Domain and Range of a Vector-Valued Function (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 288: 11.2, the domain of r(t) = f(t) i + g(t) j + h(t) k (every component defined)

blocks.text: Har function ke saath ek sawal hamesha aata hai: is mein kaun si values daal sakte hain? Isi ko domain kehte hain. Grade XI mein aap ne scalar functions ka domain nikaala tha; ab yahi kaam vector-valued function ke liye karenge, aur khushkhabri yeh hai ke koi naya formula nahin chahiye.

Kitab kehti hai: vector-valued function \(\mathbf{r}(t) = f(t)\hat{i} + g(t)\hat{j} + h(t)\hat{k}\) ka domain un tamam real numbers \(t\) ka set hai jin ke liye har component function \(f(t)\), \(g(t)\) aur \(h(t)\) defined ho (yani jin par sab ki value nikal sake).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
"Har" component kyun? \(\mathbf{r}(t)\) ek hi vector hai jo apne sab components se mil kar banta hai. Agar kisi \(t\) par ek component bhi value na de, to us \(t\) par vector likha hi nahin ja sakta, aur woh \(t\) domain se bahar hai. Ise team ki tarah samjhiye: match tabhi hoga jab sab khiladi maujood hon; ek bhi ghaaib ho to match nahin.
Har component ek aam scalar function hai, is liye Grade XI ke domain wale rules hi lagenge. Neeche table mein woh rules hain jo sab se zyada kaam aate hain.

blocks.caption: Hamara table: aam component functions kahan defined hain (n integer hai)

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Hamari taraf se misaal: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = \ln t\,\hat{i} + \sqrt{3 - t}\,\hat{j} + \dfrac{1}{t - 2}\hat{k}\).
\(\ln t\) ke liye \(t > 0\) chahiye; \(\sqrt{3 - t}\) ke liye \(3 - t \ge 0\), yani \(t \le 3\); aur \(\frac{1}{t-2}\) ke liye \(t \ne 2\). Teenon shartein ek saath poori hon:
\[t \in (0, 2) \cup (2, 3]\]
Number line par socho: pehle \(0\) se \(3\) tak ka hissa lo (\(0\) ke baghair, \(3\) ke saath), phir us mein se \(2\) nikaal do.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Khud sochiye: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = e^{t}\hat{i} + \cos t\,\hat{j}\) ka domain kya hai? Dono components har real \(t\) par defined hain, is liye domain poori real line \(\mathbb{R}\) hai.
Agla page (11.2.1) yahi kaam do steps mein likhta hai aur range ki definition bhi deta hai; wahan kitab ki ek poori misaal hal karenge.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(\mathbf{r}(t)\) ka domain = woh tamam real \(t\) jin par har component defined ho.
2. Pehle har component ka domain alag nikaalo, phir sirf woh \(t\) rakho jo sab mein common hon.
3. Square root: andar \(\ge 0\); fraction: denominator \(\ne 0\); \(\ln\): andar \(> 0\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Component domains ko jor dena (union), jab ke common hissa (intersection) lena hota hai.
2. Jo component har \(t\) par defined hai, woh koi pabandi nahin lagata; us ki wajah se domain chhota nahin hota.
3. \(\ln t\) ko \(t \ge 0\) par defined samajhna: \(\ln 0\) defined nahin, is liye \(t > 0\).
